chunks: Among what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn Nu'aym al-Sahhaf, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: The mother of my child sees blood while she is pregnant; what should she do regarding the salat (prayer)? He said:

If the pregnant woman sees blood after twenty days have passed from the time in the month when she used to see blood, the month in which she used to refrain, then that is not from the womb and not menstruation; so let her perform wudu (ablution), insert cotton, and pray. But if the pregnant woman sees blood shortly before the time when she used to see blood, or at that time in that month, then it is from menstruation; so let her refrain from salat (prayer) for the number of days she used to refrain during her menstrual days. If the blood stops before that, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) and pray. And if the blood does not stop until a day or two after the days in which she used to see blood have passed, then let her perform ghusl, insert cotton, bind herself, and pray al-Zuhr and al-'Asr. Then let her observe: if the blood between that and al-Maghrib does not flow beyond the back of the cotton, then let her perform wudu (ablution) and pray at the time of every salat (prayer) so long as she has not removed the cotton. But if she removes the cotton and the blood flows, ghusl becomes obligatory upon her. And if she removes the cotton and the blood does not flow, then let her perform wudu (ablution) and pray, and there is no ghusl upon her.

He said: If the blood, when she holds the cotton, flows from behind the cotton in a pouring manner and does not cease, then she must perform ghusl three times in every day and night, insert cotton, and pray: she performs ghusl for al-Fajr, performs ghusl for al-Zuhr and al-'Asr, and performs ghusl for al-Maghrib and al-'Isha'. He said: And likewise does the woman in istihadah; for when she does that, Allah removes the blood from her.

key_terms.الدَّمَ: the blood seen, whose legal classification determines the ruling
key_terms.الْحَامِلُ: the pregnant woman whose bleeding rulings are being discussed
key_terms.الْحَيْضَةِ: the menstrual period treated as hayd in law
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in certain states of bleeding
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفِ: cotton used to check or contain the bleeding
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: the woman experiencing istihadah, or non-menstrual irregular bleeding

ai.seo_question: What should a pregnant woman do if she sees blood with regard to salat (prayer) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for a pregnant woman who sees blood, distinguishing between blood treated as hayd and blood treated as istihadah based on timing and flow. It explains when she must refrain from salat (prayer), when she should perform wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath), and how to manage continuing bleeding during worship.
